```{r}
# 1. SETUP — Install and load required packages

# Core package list
required_packages <- c(
  "tidyverse",
  "readxl",
  "plm",
  "lmtest",
  "sandwich",
  "modelsummary",
  "ggplot2",
  "countrycode",
  "zoo",
  "scales",
  "gt",
  "kableExtra"
)

# Install missing packages only
installed <- rownames(installed.packages())
missing_packages <- setdiff(required_packages, installed)

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  install.packages(missing_packages)
}

# Load packages
invisible(lapply(required_packages, library, character.only = TRUE))
```


```{r}
# 2. LOAD RAW DATA

# Set the path to your data folder — adjust if needed
data_path <- "data/"

# ---- 2a. Homicide rate (UNODC) ----
# Source: UNODC Statistics — Intentional Homicide
# Sheet: data_cts_intentional_homicide
# Unit: Rate per 100,000 population, Total sex, Total age, Total dimension

hom_raw <- read_excel(
  path  = paste0(data_path, "homicide_data.xlsx"),
  sheet = "data_cts_intentional_homicide",
  skip  = 2        # first 2 rows are metadata/header info
)

# ---- 2b. Gini coefficient (World Bank PIP) ----
# Source: World Bank Poverty & Inequality Platform
# Format: wide — one column per year labelled "YYYY [YRYYYY]"

gini_raw <- read_csv(
  file = paste0(data_path, "gini_Data.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# ---- 2c. GDP per capita (World Bank WDI) ----
# Source: World Bank — NY.GDP.PCAP.KD (constant 2015 USD)
# Format: wide with 4 header rows; skip first 4

gdppc_raw <- read_csv(
  file      = paste0(data_path, "gdppc_data.csv"),
  skip      = 4,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# ---- 2d. Population (World Bank WDI) ----
# Source: World Bank — SP.POP.TOTL
# Same wide format as GDP

pop_raw <- read_csv(
  file      = paste0(data_path, "pop_data.csv"),
  skip      = 4,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# ---- 2e. Democracy Index (EIU via World Bank DATA360) ----
# Source: EIU Democracy Index, scores 0-10
# Format: long — one row per country-year

di_raw <- read_csv(
  file = paste0(data_path, "DI.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```


```{r}
# 3. CLEAN AND RESHAPE EACH DATASET

# ---- 3a. Homicide ----
hom <- hom_raw %>%
  # Keep only: total rate (not counts), total sex, total age, total dimension
  filter(
    `Unit of measurement` == "Rate per 100,000 population",
    Sex       == "Total",
    Age       == "Total",
    Dimension == "Total"
  ) %>%
  select(iso3 = Iso3_code, country = Country, year = Year, homicide_rate = VALUE) %>%
  mutate(
    year          = as.integer(year),
    homicide_rate = as.numeric(homicide_rate)
  ) %>%
  # Restrict to our study window
  filter(year >= 2006, year <= 2023)

cat("Homicide: ", nrow(hom), "rows,", n_distinct(hom$iso3), "countries\n")


# ---- 3b. Gini ----
# Wide to long — year columns are named "YYYY [YRYYYY]"
year_cols_gini <- names(gini_raw)[grepl("YR", names(gini_raw))]

gini <- gini_raw %>%
  select(`Country Name`, `Country Code`, all_of(year_cols_gini)) %>%
  rename(country = `Country Name`, iso3 = `Country Code`) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = all_of(year_cols_gini),
    names_to  = "year_label",
    values_to = "gini"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Extract 4-digit year from "2005 [YR2005]"
    year = as.integer(str_extract(year_label, "^[0-9]{4}")),
    gini = as.numeric(na_if(gini, ".."))   # World Bank uses ".." for missing
  ) %>%
  select(iso3, year, gini) %>%
  filter(year >= 2006, year <= 2023)

cat("Gini (before interpolation):", sum(!is.na(gini$gini)), "non-null values\n")


# ---- 3c. GDP per capita ----
year_cols_wb <- as.character(2006:2023)

gdppc <- gdppc_raw %>%
  select(`Country Code`, all_of(year_cols_wb)) %>%
  rename(iso3 = `Country Code`) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = all_of(year_cols_wb),
    names_to  = "year",
    values_to = "gdppc"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year  = as.integer(year),
    gdppc = as.numeric(gdppc)
  )

cat("GDP per capita:", sum(!is.na(gdppc$gdppc)), "non-null values\n")


# ---- 3d. Population ----
pop <- pop_raw %>%
  select(`Country Code`, all_of(year_cols_wb)) %>%
  rename(iso3 = `Country Code`) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = all_of(year_cols_wb),
    names_to  = "year",
    values_to = "pop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(year),
    pop  = as.numeric(pop)
  )

cat("Population:", sum(!is.na(pop$pop)), "non-null values\n")


# ---- 3e. Democracy Index ----
di <- di_raw %>%
  select(
    iso3       = REF_AREA,
    year       = TIME_PERIOD,
    democracy  = OBS_VALUE
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year      = as.integer(year),
    democracy = as.numeric(democracy)
  ) %>%
  filter(year >= 2006, year <= 2023)

cat("Democracy Index:", nrow(di), "rows,", n_distinct(di$iso3), "countries\n")
```


```{r}
# 4. MERGE ALL DATASETS

panel <- hom %>%
  left_join(gini,  by = c("iso3", "year")) %>%
  left_join(gdppc, by = c("iso3", "year")) %>%
  left_join(pop,   by = c("iso3", "year")) %>%
  left_join(di,    by = c("iso3", "year"))

cat("\nMerged panel:", nrow(panel), "rows,", n_distinct(panel$iso3), "countries\n")
```


```{r}
# 5. DATA TRANSFORMATIONS

# ---- 5a. Interpolate Gini within-country ----
# The Gini coefficient is surveyed irregularly (every 2-5 years).
# Linear interpolation within country is standard practice in the
# cross-country inequality literature (Fajnzylber et al., 2002).
# We only interpolate — never extrapolate beyond observed values.

panel <- panel %>%
  arrange(iso3, year) %>%
  group_by(iso3) %>%
  mutate(
    gini_interp = zoo::na.approx(gini, na.rm = FALSE)  # interpolate only
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("Gini after interpolation:", sum(!is.na(panel$gini_interp)), "non-null values\n")


# ---- 5b. Log transformations ----
# Both homicide_rate and gdppc are right-skewed. Log transformation
# reduces outlier influence and allows % interpretation of coefficients.
# Consistent with Fajnzylber et al. (2002) and Kelly (2000).

panel <- panel %>%
  mutate(
    log_homicide = log(homicide_rate + 0.01),  # +0.01 avoids log(0) for rare zero cases
    log_gdppc    = log(gdppc)
  )


# ---- 5c. Interaction term for secondary hypothesis ----
# H2: democracy moderates the inequality-crime relationship.
# We centre both variables before interacting to reduce multicollinearity.

panel <- panel %>%
  mutate(
    gini_c       = gini_interp - mean(gini_interp, na.rm = TRUE),
    democracy_c  = democracy   - mean(democracy,   na.rm = TRUE),
    gini_x_dem   = gini_c * democracy_c
  )
```


```{r}
# 6. SAMPLE RESTRICTIONS

panel_clean <- panel %>%
  
  # (1) Remove microstates (population < 500,000)
  filter(is.na(pop) | pop >= 500000) %>%
  
  # (2) Keep only rows with available interpolated Gini
  filter(!is.na(gini_interp)) %>%
  
  # (3) Drop rows missing GDP or democracy
  filter(!is.na(log_gdppc), !is.na(democracy)) %>%
  
  # (4) Remove countries where the maximum gap between actual
  #     (non-missing) Gini observations exceeds 5 years
  group_by(iso3) %>%
  mutate(
    # Years where original (non-interpolated) Gini is observed
    observed_year = ifelse(!is.na(gini), year, NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    max_gap = {
      yrs <- observed_year[!is.na(observed_year)]
      if (length(yrs) <= 1) {
        Inf   # no or only one real observation -> unreliable
      } else {
        max(diff(yrs))
      }
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(max_gap <= 5) %>%
  select(iso3) %>%
  inner_join(
    panel %>%
      filter(is.na(pop) | pop >= 500000) %>%
      filter(!is.na(gini_interp)) %>%
      filter(!is.na(log_gdppc), !is.na(democracy)),
    by = "iso3"
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("\n=== FINAL CLEAN SAMPLE ===\n")
cat("Observations:", nrow(panel_clean), "\n")
cat("Countries:   ", dplyr::n_distinct(panel_clean$iso3), "\n")
cat("Year range:  ", min(panel_clean$year), "-", max(panel_clean$year), "\n")
```

# 8. DATA VISUALISATIONS — PUBLICATION-QUALITY AESTHETICS

# Custom publication theme
theme_pub <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13, base_family = "Helvetica") +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 16,
        margin = margin(b = 8)
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 11,
        colour = "grey30",
        margin = margin(b = 10)
      ),
      plot.caption = element_text(
        size = 9,
        colour = "grey40",
        hjust = 0
      ),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(colour = "grey20"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
        colour = "grey88",
        linewidth = 0.4
      ),
      plot.background = element_rect(
        fill = "white",
        colour = NA
      ),
      panel.background = element_rect(
        fill = "white",
        colour = NA
      ),
      plot.margin = margin(15, 20, 15, 15)
    )
}

# Consistent color palette
col_blue   <- "#2C7FB8"
col_green  <- "#1B9E77"
col_orange <- "#E67E22"
col_purple <- "#5E3C99"
col_gray   <- "#4D4D4D"

```{r}
# 9. PANEL REGRESSION MODELS

# Convert to pdata.frame for plm (panel data)
pdata <- pdata.frame(panel_clean, index = c("iso3", "year"))


# ---- Model 1: Pooled OLS (baseline) ----
# No fixed effects — benchmark model, likely biased due to omitted country traits
m1 <- plm(
  log_homicide ~ gini_interp + log_gdppc + democracy,
  data   = pdata,
  model  = "pooling"
)


# ---- Model 2: Country Fixed Effects ----
# Controls for all time-invariant country characteristics (culture, geography, etc.)
m2 <- plm(
  log_homicide ~ gini_interp + log_gdppc + democracy,
  data   = pdata,
  model  = "within",
  effect = "individual"   # country FE only
)


# ---- Model 3: Two-Way Fixed Effects (country + year) ----
# Also controls for global shocks affecting all countries in a given year
# (e.g. 2008 financial crisis, COVID-19 in 2020)
m3 <- plm(
  log_homicide ~ gini_interp + log_gdppc + democracy,
  data   = pdata,
  model  = "within",
  effect = "twoways"   # country + year FE
)


# ---- Model 4: Two-Way FE + Interaction (secondary hypothesis) ----
# Tests H2: does democracy moderate the inequality-crime relationship?
m4 <- plm(
  log_homicide ~ gini_interp + log_gdppc + democracy + gini_x_dem,
  data   = pdata,
  model  = "within",
  effect = "twoways"
)


# ---- Hausman Test: FE vs RE ----
# H0: random effects are consistent (use RE)
# If p < 0.05: reject H0, fixed effects preferred
m2_re <- plm(
  log_homicide ~ gini_interp + log_gdppc + democracy,
  data   = pdata,
  model  = "random"
)

hausman_test <- phtest(m2, m2_re)
cat("\n=== HAUSMAN TEST ===\n")
print(hausman_test)
```


```{r}
# 10. CLUSTERED STANDARD ERRORS

# We cluster SEs at the country level to account for serial correlation
# within countries over time (Bertrand, Duflo, Mullainathan, 2004)

cluster_se <- function(model, data = pdata) {
  coeftest(model, vcov = vcovHC(model, type = "HC1", cluster = "group"))
}

m1_se <- cluster_se(m1)
m2_se <- cluster_se(m2)
m3_se <- cluster_se(m3)
m4_se <- cluster_se(m4)

# Print main model results
cat("\n=== MODEL 3: Two-Way FE (Main Model) ===\n")
print(m3_se)

cat("\n=== MODEL 4: Two-Way FE + Interaction ===\n")
print(m4_se)
```


```{r}
# 11. PUBLICATION-QUALITY REGRESSION TABLE

# Cluster-robust variance-covariance matrices
vcov_list <- list(
  vcovHC(m1, method = "arellano", type = "HC1", cluster = "group"),
  vcovHC(m2, method = "arellano", type = "HC1", cluster = "group"),
  vcovHC(m3, method = "arellano", type = "HC1", cluster = "group"),
  vcovHC(m4, method = "arellano", type = "HC1", cluster = "group")
)

# Model labels
model_list <- list(
  "Pooled OLS"               = m1,
  "Country FE"               = m2,
  "Two-Way FE"               = m3,
  "FE + Interaction"         = m4
)

# Create a beautifully formatted GT table
reg_table <- modelsummary(
  models = model_list,
  vcov = vcov_list,

  # significance stars
  stars = c("*" = 0.10, "**" = 0.05, "***" = 0.01),

  # rename coefficients
  coef_rename = c(
    "gini_interp" = "Gini coefficient",
    "log_gdppc"   = "Log GDP per capita",
    "democracy"   = "Democracy index",
    "gini_x_dem"  = "Gini × Democracy"
  ),

  # cleaner goodness-of-fit section
  gof_map = tribble(
    ~raw,         ~clean,         ~fmt,
    "nobs",       "Observations", 0,
    "r.squared",  "R²",           3,
    "adj.r.squared", "Adjusted R²", 3
  ),

  gof_omit = "AIC|BIC|Log|F$|RMSE",

  # display estimate with stars and SE in parentheses
  estimate  = "{estimate}{stars}",
  statistic = "({std.error})",

  # use GT for modern styling
  output = "gt"
)


# Style the table (ASCII-safe text only)
reg_table_styled <- reg_table %>%
  gt::tab_header(
    title = gt::md("**Table 2. Income Inequality and Homicide Rates**"),
    subtitle = gt::md("Panel Regression Results, 2006-2023")
  ) %>%
  gt::tab_source_note(
    source_note = gt::md(
      "Cluster-robust standard errors (country level) in parentheses.<br>
      *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.10.<br>
      Dependent variable: Log homicide rate per 100,000 population."
    )
  ) %>%
  gt::opt_row_striping() %>%
  gt::tab_options(
    table.font.names = c("Times New Roman", "Georgia", "serif"),
    table.font.size = gt::px(13),
    heading.title.font.size = gt::px(18),
    heading.subtitle.font.size = gt::px(12),
    source_notes.font.size = gt::px(10),
    data_row.padding = gt::px(5)
  )

# Display in RStudio Viewer
print(reg_table_styled)

# Save to HTML
gt::gtsave(
  reg_table_styled,
  filename = "regression_table.html"
)

# Also save as Word using modelsummary directly
modelsummary(
  models = model_list,
  vcov = vcov_list,
  stars = c("*" = 0.10, "**" = 0.05, "***" = 0.01),
  coef_rename = c(
    "gini_interp" = "Gini coefficient",
    "log_gdppc"   = "Log GDP per capita",
    "democracy"   = "Democracy index",
    "gini_x_dem"  = "Gini x Democracy"
  ),
  estimate  = "{estimate}{stars}",
  statistic = "({std.error})",
  gof_omit  = "AIC|BIC|Log|F$|RMSE",
  title = "Table 2. Income Inequality and Homicide Rates",
  notes = c(
    "Cluster-robust standard errors (country level) in parentheses.",
    "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.10.",
    "Dependent variable: Log homicide rate per 100,000 population."
  ),
  output = "regression_table.docx"
)

cat("Files saved:\n")
cat("- regression_table.html\n")
cat("- regression_table.docx\n")
```


```{r}
# 12. ROBUSTNESS CHECKS

# ---- 12a. Alternative dependent variable: regional homicide estimates ----
# Use UNODC's regional estimates sheet as an alternative measure
hom_reg_raw <- read_excel(
  path  = paste0(data_path, "homicide_data.xlsx"),
  sheet = "data_cts_homicide_reg_estimates",
  skip  = 2
)

# ---- 12b. Exclude outlier countries with extremely high homicide rates ----
# Countries with homicide rate > 60 per 100,000 (e.g. El Salvador in peak years)
# may unduly influence results

panel_no_outliers <- panel_clean %>%
  filter(homicide_rate <= 60)

pdata_robust <- pdata.frame(panel_no_outliers, index = c("iso3", "year"))

m3_robust <- plm(
  log_homicide ~ gini_interp + log_gdppc + democracy,
  data   = pdata_robust,
  model  = "within",
  effect = "twoways"
)

cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS: Two-Way FE excluding extreme outliers ===\n")
print(coeftest(m3_robust, vcov = vcovHC(m3_robust, type = "HC1", cluster = "group")))

```
